introH2: 🛕 Can you do Chachoengsao on a budget — and which area is best value?
introHtml: Chachoengsao (Paet Riu) is a town close to Bangkok that many people visit on a day trip to pay respects at Wat Sothon and explore the Bang Pakong riverfront — but staying overnight lets you soak up the riverside-town feel far more, and the good news is there are more well-scored stays in the ฿500s–800s here than most people expect. The key to doing Paet Riu on a budget is to pick the area that matches your plans, because the cheaper stays are spread around — the town centre (Mueang Chachoengsao) is near Wat Sothon, the markets, the railway station and the 100-year-old Ban Mai market, best for temple visits, market strolls and travellers without a car; Bang Pakong district is near the Wellgrow industrial estate and the river mouth, handy for workers or a stopover; and the outskirts have quiet garden stays for self-drivers. Many people book without checking the area and end up driving back and forth to Wat Sothon several times. This guide rounds up 10 budget Chachoengsao stays we've reviewed, every one scoring 8.0+ — all drawn from real guest reviews, with honest pros and cons, prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Chachoengsao has no metro, but it's very close to Bangkok — about a 1–1.5 hour drive — and the eastern-line railway station sits in the town centre, so you can easily arrive by train from Krung Thep Aphiwat/Hua Lamphong and visit Wat Sothon without driving. Pick by your itinerary for the best value: the town centre (Na Mueang–Sothon) is near Wat Sothon, the station, the markets and the 100-year-old Ban Mai market, best if you don't have a car (Kesorn, BB House, Heaven, JK Living, Yenjit, Sunee View, Malone); Bang Phra is on the Mueang Chachoengsao side, drivable to town and Wat Sothon (The Wish); and Bang Pakong–Phimpha sits near the Wellgrow estate and the river mouth, handy for a stopover or workers (Wellgrow). Almost every stay here has free parking, so they suit self-drivers well — the Bang Pakong and outskirts stays are easiest with a car, as public transport is limited.

entries.name: Heaven Hotel Chachoengsao
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chachoengsao-Bang Pakong Rd · Na Mueang · near Wat Sothon
entries.addr: Chachoengsao-Bang Pakong Rd, Na Mueang, Mueang Chachoengsao
entries.storyHtml: Heaven Hotel is the most well-rounded value pick in this guide — 9.2 from 129 reviews, the highest score and most reviews among the budget tier. Opened in 2020, the rooms are still fresh and clean, sitting on Chachoengsao-Bang Pakong Road in town, a few minutes' drive to Wat Sothon and walkable to markets and restaurants. Room types run from a Superior at ฿790 up to a Family Room, suiting couples, families and anyone staying overnight for a temple visit — all for under a thousand baht.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Visit Wat Sothon early before the crowds — it's only a few minutes' drive from here. If your budget stretches, pick a Deluxe, which is roomier and newer than the Superior.

entries.storyHtml: Kesorn Boutique is the lowest-priced stay in this guide — from just ฿550 — yet it scores a high 8.7 from 60 reviews. It's a small boutique stay on Suk Prayun Road in town, near Wat Sothon and walkable to markets and restaurants. Rooms are around 20 sq m with air-con, TV and hot water, in both double and twin layouts — ideal for budget travellers who just want a clean, well-placed in-town room for an overnight temple visit.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Some of the cheapest Knockdown rooms have no window — for a brighter room pick a Standard Double/Twin with a window, only a hundred-odd baht more.

entries.storyHtml: Wellgrow Service House is a budget stay near the Wellgrow industrial estate with a high 9.1 score from 27 reviews. It's in Phimpha subdistrict of Bang Pakong, on a main road, with rooms around 24 sq m that include a work desk and a rain shower — from just ฿700. It suits both estate workers and travellers breaking up a Bangkok–east-coast drive, giving you a spacious, clean room at a friendly price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's on a main road — ask for a garden-view room on the inner side, which is quieter than the road side. Shops nearby are sparse, so pick up food in town first. It books direct on Agoda and Trip.com.

entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you work at the estate or need several nights, ask the property directly about the monthly rate — it works out cheaper than booking nightly.

entries.storyHtml: Yenjit Resort is a leafy bungalow resort in town, only about 200 m — a 9-minute walk — from Chachoengsao railway station, scoring 8.9 from 30 reviews. Reviewers praise the shady, quiet grounds, the spacious clean rooms, and a free breakfast buffet that's well put together and changes daily. Rates start at ฿800 with free parking, and Tripadvisor ranks it #1 in Chachoengsao — ideal for train travellers who want a quiet in-town stay.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Arriving by train is the best value — you can walk from the station. Don't miss the free breakfast buffet (07:00–10:00). If you drive a larger car, go slow at the fairly narrow lane entrance.

entries.storyHtml: Suanmaithara Resort is a quiet garden resort about 8 minutes' drive from Wat Sothon, scoring 8.8 from 64 reviews. It's a cluster of around 20 rooms set among gardens with parking right outside each room and a leafy feel cut off from road noise. Room types run from a Standard at ฿800 up to VIP and a family room — ideal for self-drivers who want peace and quiet while still being able to drive into town and reach Wat Sothon easily.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Couples wanting a more spacious room should pick the VIP Room, the largest here; families should go for the family room with an extra bed.

entries.storyHtml: Sunee View Hotel is a small, quiet hotel in Sothon subdistrict, only about 1 km from Wat Sothon — close enough to walk, scoring 8.2. The Deluxe Studio rooms are clean with a fridge, TV and air-con, some with a balcony, and there's a garden to sit in, bikes to borrow and a little fishing spot, all from just ฿550. Ideal for pilgrims and self-drivers who want a clean room near the temple at a low price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you like a softer bed, ask for a mattress topper at check-in. For a balcony room, request it when booking — not every room has one.

entries.storyHtml: The Wish Hotel is the newly opened hotel with the most reviews in this guide — 146, scoring 8.1. It's a 64-room hotel in Bang Phra subdistrict, and its standout point is that every room has a private balcony; the rooms are still new and clean, with rates from just ฿850. It sits on the Bang Phra side of Mueang Chachoengsao, within driving distance of town and Wat Sothon — ideal for self-drivers who want a new, heavily reviewed hotel at a friendly price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Every room has a balcony — ask for a higher floor for an open view and more quiet. If your budget stretches, the King Room is notably roomier than the Deluxe.

entries.storyHtml: Malone Maranatha is the only Arabian-Moroccan-style boutique hotel in town, a colourful building on Sothon Phatthana Road about 3.5 km from the centre, near Wat Sothon and Robinson, scoring 8.0. It has around 24–25 clean, new-looking rooms with free Wi-Fi and parking, plus a barbecue area to hang out in, from ฿700. Ideal for anyone who wants a clean room with a distinctive look at a friendly price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Check at booking whether the rate includes the English breakfast. If you like opening a window for fresh air, ask to see the room first — the building's design means some windows don't open easily.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates in the off-peak season and may change by date and season — always check live rates and compare 3 sites before booking. Scores and highlights here are drawn from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, not from staying ourselves. Every stay in this set scores 8.0 or above but is a budget 2–3 star, so there are trade-offs for the price — most have no pool, some Kesorn rooms have no window, and Wellgrow sits on the Bang Pakong side away from the town centre; please read each stay's caveats before booking. Wellgrow Service House doesn't have a dedicated Booking.com page yet, so it can be compared on Agoda and Trip.com; the other 9 can be compared across all 3 sites. During the Luang Pho Sothon worship festival and long weekends, in-town hotels fill fast and prices rise, so book ahead. Chachoengsao has no metro but is close to Bangkok, about a 1–1.5 hour drive, with an eastern-line railway station in the town centre. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about budget Chachoengsao hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which budget Chachoengsao stay is the best value?
faq.a: For value (score per baht), Kesorn Boutique from ฿550, scoring 8.7, is the lowest-priced in this set · BB House ฿650 (scores 9.1) and Wellgrow Service House ฿700 (scores 9.1) are also great value · while the highest-scored and most-reviewed of the group is Heaven Hotel, 9.2 from 129 reviews at ฿790, in town near Wat Sothon

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget Chachoengsao hotels cost?
faq.a: In this guide prices start around ฿550–850 a night · the cheapest are Kesorn and Sunee View from ฿550, BB House ฿650, Wellgrow and Malone ฿700 · the mid-range are Heaven ฿790, Suanmaithara and Yenjit ฿800, JK Living ฿806 and The Wish ฿850 · all are approximate off-peak rates that rise noticeably during the Wat Sothon festival and long weekends

faq.q: ❓ Visiting Wat Sothon — which stay is closest?
faq.a: The closest, close enough to walk, is Sunee View Hotel (฿550), about 1 km from Wat Sothon · in-town stays a few minutes' drive from the temple and walkable to markets are Heaven Hotel (฿790, scores 9.2), BB House (฿650) and Kesorn Boutique (฿550, cheapest) · Suanmaithara Resort (฿800) is a garden resort about 8 minutes' drive from the temple

faq.q: ❓ Arriving in Chachoengsao by train with no car — where to stay?
faq.a: Yenjit Resort (฿800) has the edge — it's only about 200 m from Chachoengsao railway station, so you can step off the train and walk to the stay · in-town options like Kesorn, BB House and Heaven are also in the town centre, walkable to markets and restaurants and a short ride from the station

faq.q: ❓ Do any budget Chachoengsao hotels have a pool?
faq.a: The budget stays in this set (boutiques, guesthouses, garden resorts) mostly have no pool, as they focus on location and price · if you want a Chachoengsao stay with a pool and spa you'll need to step up to a pricier riverside resort on the Bang Pakong, such as Suntara Wellness Resort, which appears in our Top 12 Chachoengsao Hotels guide

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest to book a Chachoengsao hotel?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary by promotion and period, so open and compare all 3 before booking every time — 9 of the 10 stays here can be compared across all 3 sites, while Wellgrow Service House doesn't have a dedicated Booking.com page yet, so it's on Agoda and Trip.com · each review page has the comparison links, which can save you tens to hundreds of baht a night
